row.notes: add rcx,0x18 (4 bytes) in Sess_InGameRace_Update (+0x770), the join of the driver name block of the car_retirement HUD message. The block finds the retired car's entrant: gm = [[rdi+0xca0]+0x88]+0x260, the 0x88-byte entrant list [gm+0x2e0..+0x2e8) searched for byte +0x82 == r15b (the vehicle index), then calls Ent_Get_Driver_Thunk (0x1423dbcf0 at 0x142d624cb, rcx = [gm+0xf78] = the entrants system, rdx = entrant+0x50 = its packed driver ref: domain byte +0x50, u16 stat id +0x52). rcx here is the driver record + 8 (0x142d624d5..0x142d624dc, jmp 0x142d624e0) or 0 from xor ecx,ecx at 0x142d624de, which six branches reach: 0x142d62478 and 0x142d62480 (vehicle index 0xff), 0x142d62493 (empty entrant list), 0x142d624b9 and 0x142d624c2 (no entrant for the vehicle) and 0x142d624d3 (the driver lookup returned 0). Next: lea rdx,[rsp+0x50] and call 0x14249ac60 (jmp 0x14cb8a5d0, the driver name fill, rcx = driver+0x20, rdx = the result string at rsp+0x50), which reads [rcx+0x1d8] at 0x14cb8a5e1 with no test, so every null path faults reading 0x1f0 (crash reports: reading 0x1f0 at F1_25.exe+0xcb8a5e1 < Sess_InGameRace_Update+0x77e with rax=0, rcx=0x18, as a car retires). Core hooks it and, for rcx == 0, writes the callee's own empty-name fallback into the result (0x14cb8a684..0x14cb8a69f: [rsp+0x50] = g_Ne_InlineStr128Vtable, [+8] = 0x80, [+0x10] = rsp+0x68, byte [+0x18] = 0; with both name pointers null the callee appends nothing more) and sets rip to site_Sess_InGameRaceRetirementDriverJoin. A 5-byte jump covers this instruction and lea rdx (9 bytes, neither relative); a 14-byte jump would take in the call's rel32 and is refused. Branch targets in the block are 0x142d624de (six) and 0x142d624e0 (the jmp at 0x142d624dc); none lands in 0x142d624e1..0x142d624ed (linear sweep of 0x142d61d70..0x142d6308b, which ends on the pdata end, no indirect jumps). A hook at 0x142d624de would put 0x142d624e0 inside its patch.
